title: ci: enforce the Rust toolchain pin instead of asking for it in a comment
body:
## The gap

The pin itself already shipped and is correct: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
1.97.1, and both `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` uses are pinned to the SHA for that
same version. What was missing was any enforcement.

The two halves **cannot reference each other** — that action does not read
toolchain files, its `@rev` *is* the version selector — so the only thing tying
them together was a comment in three files saying "bump both together". This
repo already treats a stated invariant with nothing checking it as a defect.

The failure mode is what makes it worth a check: bump the TOML alone and CI keeps
building on the old compiler; bump the action alone and every developer's machine
drifts off what CI validates. **Neither goes red on its own.** The pin just stops
meaning anything — the exact state it was created to end.

## What the check asserts

1. The channel is an exact three-part version, not a floating one (`stable`,
   `beta`, `nightly`, or a two-part `1.97` all re-introduce the drift).
2. Every `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` use under `.github/` carries a trailing
   `# <version>` comment. A bare SHA is unreviewable by construction, so that
   comment is load-bearing rather than decoration.
3. Every one of those declared versions equals the channel.
4. The Cargo MSRV is not *above* the pin — that pairing cannot compile at all.

It deliberately does **not** verify the SHA genuinely is that version: that needs
a network call, and it isn't the mistake people make. The realistic error is
updating one place and forgetting the other, which is fully catchable offline.

Wired into `lint-format`, which has no path filter and so runs on every PR — a
toolchain guard that only fired when Rust files changed would miss the case where
someone edits only the workflow. The three comments now name their enforcer
instead of asking nicely.

## Verification

Mutation-tested five ways **against the real repo**, each red, tree restored
clean each time:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| bump `rust-toolchain.toml` only (the realistic mistake) | 🔴 names both versions and both files |
| bump the action's version comment only | 🔴 |
| float the channel back to `stable` | 🔴 "not an exact version" |
| strip a version comment | 🔴 "no trailing `# <version>`" |
| raise the MSRV past the pin | 🔴 "cannot compile" |

Plus 11 black-box CLI tests over a fake repo tree, following
`check-tech-radar.test.mjs`. One covers **removing CI's pin entirely**, which
would otherwise pass vacuously — with nothing to compare, nothing disagrees.
Another checks that every use is examined rather than just the first, and another
that a `uses:` line inside a comment is treated as prose, not a pin.

`pnpm test` 479 files / 6933 tests, `lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean,
`format:check` clean.

## Note

`rust-toolchain.toml` and edition 2024 were both on the backlog as pending; both
turned out to be already done. This PR closes what was actually left of that item
— the enforcement, not the pin.

title: fix(locale): give Spain, Portugal and Brazil the profiles they were already promised
body:
Follow-up to #1007, which fixed Italy and explicitly deferred the identical gap
for Spain and Portugal. This closes it, and Brazil with it.

## The gap

All three were already live market ids **on the TS side** — `COUNTRY_TO_MARKET`
maps `ES`/`PT`/`BR`, `LANGUAGE_TO_MARKET` maps `es`/`pt` — and the Rust side had
an arm for none of them, so `LocaleProfile::get` dropped them to the
international default and `pick_locale` returned `"en"`.

The visible result was **half a localization**. `resume_conventions` already has
curated `es`/`pt` entries, so the model wrote "Experiencia profesional" and
"Formação" — and then arranged them in the American order, with `photo: Never`
and the 2-page Anglophone budget. A half-localized document reads worse than an
unlocalized one, because it matches no market's expectations at all.

## What changed

`IT_ORDER` becomes `EUROPASS_ORDER` and now serves all four markets. That is
what it always was: its own doc justified the order by pointing at Europass, not
at anything specifically Italian.

**Scope is principled, not arbitrary.** These are exactly the markets whose
section *headings* are already curated. `tr`, `ru`, `cn`, `jp` and `kr` are live
TS ids too, and they are deliberately left alone: they get English headings, so
giving them a non-English section *order* would manufacture the very
half-localized document this PR is fixing. The order axis tracks the heading
axis on purpose.

## Two per-market calls, flagged rather than asserted

- **Spain and Portugal cap at 2 pages, not Italy's 3.** Spanish guidance is
  consistently "máximo dos páginas", and this cap is advice the trim panel acts
  on, so inheriting Italy's 3 would license a longer document than the market
  expects.
- **Brazil gets `photo: Never` where Portugal gets `Optional`.** Brazilian
  hiring guidance has moved against CV photos on anti-discrimination grounds.
  Same language, same section order, different norm — which is exactly why it is
  a distinct profile rather than a `pt` alias. Both are one-line changes if a
  native reviewer disagrees.

## The test that should have caught this

`all_markets_are_distinct_and_present` asserted a hardcoded count and id list, so
it passed throughout — it could not fail for a market it did not name. It now
asserts the property instead: **every profile `all()` advertises must round-trip
through `get()` back to itself.** That is the contract the rest of the app
depends on, since `pick_locale` forwards a profile's `id` verbatim and downstream
code calls `get` on it.

Mutation-checked by deleting the `"es"` arm — the exact shape of the bug that
shipped. The new test goes red; the old one stayed green under the same mutation.

## Verification

`cargo test --all-features --locked`: 4206 lib + 18 architecture + 20 egress + 3
eval. clippy `--all-features --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean,
typecheck 13/13, `lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean, `check:agent-system` and
`check-landing-drift` green.

Four mutations run, each green at baseline and red with the feature deleted:
dropping `es|pt|br` from the order arm, dropping the `"es"` `get()` arm, giving
two profiles the same id, and dropping the `es`/`pt` `pick_locale` arms.

## Not in scope

`SectionId::from_header` remains English-only — unchanged from #1007, where the
reasoning is recorded.

title: feat(scraping): add freehire as the aggregator's keyless tier
body:
Closes #1002.

## Why this, and why we wrote it ourselves

freehire's maintainer opened #1002, disclosed the interest, and offered a PR.
We publicly committed to shipping it in the next release, so this is on the
record.

It is implemented from their **published `openapi.yaml`**, not from their PR.
The reason is rights, not code quality: this repo has no CLA, so a contribution
stays under its author's copyright and cannot be relicensed, and ADR-023 names
commercial licensing as a rationale. Reading their PR and rewriting it would be
derivative — the worst of both worlds. They were invited to review ours instead,
which captures their API knowledge without putting their copyright in the tree.

## What it buys

Every other provider needs an API key. A fresh install therefore gets a
`needs-keys` skip and **zero jobs** — the aggregator board cannot do anything
until the user has been to Settings. freehire answers unauthenticated, so the
board now works out of the box.

It is not a better data source than the keyed tiers and is never preferred over
one. It runs **last**, and only a non-empty answer from it short-circuits: an
empty answer from a provider nobody chose is not evidence about the search.

## Three consequences, stated rather than buried

**`needs_keys()` is now permanently false.** A keyless tier is always
"configured", so the skip can never fire. That is the point — the skip existed
because a keyless search could only ever return nothing. Accepted cost, tested
and written down: a keyless user who finds nothing reads "no jobs found" rather
than a prompt to add keys, and the autopilot "Needs configuration" badge is
unreachable. A keyring read *fault* is still classified separately, so the one
case the old `false` protected is unaffected.

**Its failures degrade to `Ok(empty)`, never `Err`** — the only provider with
that rule. Every other one reports its failure because a stored key means the
user asked for it specifically. Nobody opted into this one, so its outage must
not become an error banner on a search the user never aimed at them. There is
no SLA and no rate-limit header of any kind (verified: no `X-RateLimit-*`, no
`Retry-After`).

**It is skipped when a configured provider failed.** Because it is always on, it
would otherwise answer in place of a revoked or rate-limited key on essentially
every failed-key search — and with `needs_keys()` false, nothing else would
report it either.

## What the review caught

The pre-PR gate returned **BLOCK** on the first draft with two reproduced HIGHs,
both fixed in the second commit:

- freehire **replaced** the sparse guessed-market hits instead of merging with
  them. Reproduced in the commonest real configuration (Adzuna-only keys, no
  country): two London-relevant hits discarded for up to fifty globally
  unfiltered ones — the guessed-market bug already fixed for Adzuna, re-entered
  through a new door. The comment justifying it was false, and false because I
  wrote it before removing `location` from the function on finding the API has
  no city parameter at all.
- freehire **swallowed the failure diagnostic** of every configured provider.
  Reproduced: three revoked keys, `BoardScrapeSummary.error` came back `None`.

Plus a false claim on the public privacy page (it said freehire runs after keyed
tiers come back "empty or failed"; an empty keyed result is decisive and returns
immediately), a test of mine that passed for the wrong reason, and stale contract
docs. All fixed — see the second commit message for the full accounting.

## Egress

`freehire.me` is in the machine-readable inventory with a `public_name`, which
made the landing drift guard **fail** until the privacy page, README and
SECURITY named it. That guard shipped in #1005 for exactly this purpose and this
is the first new egress since — it worked. ADR-0005's class 2 gained a paragraph
on why a keyless tier still belongs there.

## Verification

`cargo test --all-features --locked`: 4203 lib + 18 architecture + 20 egress + 3
eval. `pnpm test`: 478 files / 6922 tests. clippy `--all-features --all-targets`
clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean, typecheck 13/13, `lint:strict --max-warnings 0`
clean, `check:agent-system` in sync, `check-landing-drift` green.

Every behavioural guard here was mutation-checked — green at baseline, red with
the feature deleted, restored. That includes the failed-key guard, which was
**wrong on its first attempt and caught by its own test**: the guessed-market
branch records its fall-through in `adzuna_configured_failed`, so a naive
`is_some()` read a routing decision as a key failure.

One mutation claim did not survive checking and is recorded in the test rather
than quietly dropped: the ordering guard catches "moved ahead of the keyed
tiers" but would not catch "moved one rung past Jooble", because the fixture
short-circuits at Adzuna.

## Known limits

- **No city filtering.** The documented search has `countries` and facet
  parameters but no city or free-text location parameter. Folding a city into
  the full-text `q` would drop every posting that does not spell its city out,
  remote ones included, so city precision stays the keyed tiers' job.
- **`url` unvalidated and `company` uncapped**, matching Adzuna/JSearch/Jooble
  but unlike the stricter Apify sibling. No exploit reproduced (the URL sinks
  are closed by the SSRF guard and the `http(s)` allowlist), but freehire is the
  one keyless, default-on, third-party-re-aggregating tier, so it is flagged for
  an owner call rather than silently accepted.
- The request carries the shared default user-agent, so the traffic is not
  attributable to freehire's own integration. Attribution versus fingerprinting
  is a product decision, not a defect — raising it here rather than deciding it.

title: fix(resume): localize every section heading, not the first four
body:
## The bug

A German résumé rendered **Projekte** and **Ausbildung & Sprachen** as ordinary
body text instead of section headings — owner-reported, screenshot-confirmed.
Profil, Kenntnisse, Berufserfahrung and Ausbildung looked right; everything
below did not.

Two independent halves, both required:

**Producer.** `ResumeConventions.headers` covered exactly 4 of the 9 ordered
`SectionId`s. The other five — Projects, Certifications, Languages, Awards,
Publications — were handed to the model as their raw English `SectionId` debug
word inside the "Sections run in this order" list, while the same prompt told it
to write German. The model did the reasonable thing and invented its own German
words. `headers` is now a **total record** over all nine ids in every locale, so
the TS typecheck refuses to build a locale that leaves one unnamed.

**Recogniser.** Nothing in `export::parser`'s `SECTION_NAMES` knew "Projekte",
so on the re-parse it was a paragraph, not a heading. 27 localized headings
added, plus an `"X & Y"` arm for the merged shape models emit often enough that
the draft prompt already has a rule against it.

Italy came along for the ride because `pick_locale` forwards the id verbatim and
`section_order_for` matches the literal `"it"`: without a real `LocaleProfile`,
an Italian user silently got the US section order. `IT_ORDER` runs Languages
before Skills — the one position it deliberately does not mirror the German
order, following Europass. Flagged as a reviewable call, not copied.

## Review round

A pre-PR pass found three guards on this branch that could not fail for the
reason they were written:

- the producer/recogniser guard hardcoded **both** axes its doc said it
  enumerated, so a locale added on the TS side was never visited;
- `header()` falls back to the English word rather than panicking, and nothing
  tied the TS id union to the ids `section_order_for` emits — adding
  `SectionId::Volunteer` to an order const put the literal word "Volunteer" into
  a prompt demanding Italian with every gate green;
- the collision sweep named its cases as literals and missed three of the four
  German words this branch adds.

All three now enumerate generated data. The rewrite found a **live pre-existing
defect**: Portuguese `Competências` classified as `Other`, so a pt résumé
generated by this app did not recognise its own skills section — the `ê` blocks
the `competenc` stem exactly as `z` blocked it for Italian.

It also found that `isKnownSectionName` never gained the `" & "` arm Rust has.
The shared section-names fixture compares two name *lists* and is structurally
blind to a rule that combines two entries, so the TS mirror answered `false` for
every merged heading with all tests green. Mirrored, with a new shared
`section-name-joins.json` pinning the *predicate* on both sides.

Two guard drafts were wrong on first run and are worth naming, since both are
the shape this repo keeps shipping:

- `header(id) != id` reads as a fallback for French **Certifications**, which is
  correctly spelled the same as English. Membership of the key is the property
  that actually separates a translation from a miss. The inequality form failed
  on `fr` the first time it ran.
- the collision sweep initially allowed `want || Other`, which made it unable to
  fail — a heading the recogniser does not know reads identically to one it
  knows correctly. Measured: every bucketed id already lands on its own bucket
  in all 7 locales, so the slack bought nothing.

Every guard here was mutation-checked — green at baseline, red with the feature
deleted, restored.

## Verification

`cargo test --all-features --locked`: 4191 lib + 18 architecture + 20 egress + 3
eval. `pnpm test`: 478 files / 6922 tests. clippy `--all-features --all-targets`
clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `gen:prompts:check` up to date, typecheck 13/13,
`lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean, `check:agent-system` in sync.

## Deliberately out of scope

- `SectionId::from_header` stays English-only. A localized heading becomes
  `Custom` and keeps its position, so there is no silent reorder — note that
  this does **not** hold for English joins: `"Skills & Certifications"` maps to
  `Skills`, which predates this branch and is not made worse by it.
- Spain and Portugal have the same missing-`LocaleProfile` gap Italy had.
- A newly-recognized heading with **no body under it** is now dropped rather
  than kept as body text (`push_nonempty_section`). The lost line is a bare
  label the prompt itself calls worse than no heading at all.

title: refactor(platform): own the test data-dir override where the rule says it belongs
body:
Follow-up to #1005 — one commit that missed the merge. The Stop-gate arch guard flags `std::env::var` in `linkedin_ssrf_test.rs`, which is live on `main` right now.

## The disagreement

Two guards enforce R4 and they disagree about the same file:

- `tests/architecture.rs::r4_env_access_only_in_platform` filters `!f.is_test`, so a file named `*_test.rs` is **exempt** — which is why `cargo test --test architecture` passes 18/18.
- The Stop-gate ast-grep matcher has no such exemption, so it blocks.

The gate is right in spirit. `platform/config.rs`'s own module doc says it is *"the **sole owner** of the application data-directory env var"* and that *"no other module may read"* it — so the rule was enforceable everywhere except the one place a test would actually reach for the variable.

## The fix

Rather than argue the exemption or add an allowlist entry, the override moved to where the rule points. `platform::config::DataDirGuard` is a test-only RAII scope: a caller names a **directory**, never the variable. The test file now contains no env access and does not name the variable in prose either, so both matchers are satisfied for the right reason.

Two things it improves beyond silencing the gate:

- **Restores on `Drop`**, not at the end of the test body. The previous inline version restored after the `await` but before the assertions — a panicking assertion would have leaked the override into whatever ran next.
- **`#[serial]` added to `data_dir_honors_env_then_falls_back`.** It mutates the same process-global variable directly with no serialization, so it could race the new test. Pre-existing, but only became reachable once a second test started scoping that variable.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` · `cargo test --all-features --locked` → **4169 lib + 18 architecture + 20 egress + 3 eval**, 0 failed. `grep -c "std::env"` on the test file: **0**.

title: feat: make the egress inventory testable, and close two holes found doing it
body:
Track D of the architecture-hardening audit — *"make the egress inventory testable, the cheapest high-value item in the whole audit"* — plus two security bugs found while mapping it.

## Why

ADR-0005 enumerates eight permitted egress classes in prose. Nothing was machine-readable, so a new outbound host could ship undeclared — and a 2026-07 full-history audit had already found README and SECURITY **literally false** about the app's network behaviour once. The next queued task adds `freehire.me` as an aggregator tier, and its own notes say *"declare the new outbound host in ADR-0005's egress inventory AND the landing privacy page — this is exactly the drift D1 exists to make impossible."*

## Two security bugs found on the way

**A CDN script sharing an origin with a real GitHub token.** `apps/landing/public/benchmarks/index.html` loaded `chart.js@2.9.2` from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` with no SRI, same-origin as `localStorage['ajh-mc-gh-token']`. Files under `public/` are copied verbatim by the static export, so they never pass through `ClientScripts.tsx`'s fail-closed `isAllowedScriptSrc` guard, and `CspMeta` renders only on the mission-control route — so no CSP covered that page either. Now vendored same-origin at **2.9.4**, which also clears CVE-2020-7746 (prototype pollution in `helpers.merge`) that 2.9.2 carries. Bytes verified against the registry's signed integrity field before being trusted; `check 9` pins the sha256 so a silent re-vendor fails CI, since vendoring removes the file from `pnpm audit` permanently.

**SSRF in profile import.** `detect_platform` matched `url.to_lowercase().contains("linkedin.com/in/")` over the *whole* URL, so `https://attacker.example/linkedin.com/in/x` classified as LinkedIn — and `linkedin.rs` then fetched it with `net::http::shared()` rather than `get_guarded`, whose own tests reject loopback, private ranges and the cloud-metadata literal. `http://127.0.0.1:9200/linkedin.com/in/x` reached that service. Now matches on the parsed host (exact, or dot-bounded suffix so `evillinkedin.com` fails) and fetches through `get_guarded_following_redirects`, which re-validates every hop. `scraping::scrape_url` already did it this way; this call site just never did. `github.rs` was checked and does **not** share the defect — its host is hardcoded and the username regex-validated before interpolation.

## The inventory

`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/egress.rs` — 57 `EGRESS` rows plus `SCHEMELESS` and `UNEXTRACTABLE`, seeded by **running** the extractor rather than transcribing it (the design's own hand-count was wrong twice). It scans `src/**` as text plus the three machine-readable declaration files via `include_str!`, so moving one is a compile error. Four assertions: an extracted host must be declared, a declared host must still exist, dynamic-host sites are keyed on `(path, literal)`, and CSP/manifest sources may not be a bare scheme or wildcard.

**What it does not prove is in the file header.** Every row is a *first hop* — `net/http.rs` follows up to 10 redirects and blocks only private-IP literals, so a 302 to an undeclared host is followed. Runtime-configurable provider base URLs, scheme-less host consts and hosts inside stripped `#[cfg(test)]` mods are outside it, each recorded as an accepted hole rather than papered over.

Sentry is the interesting row: its ingest host lives inside a DSN injected from a CI secret via `option_env!`, so no literal exists in any reproducible build. It sits in a separate `UNEXTRACTABLE` list — a placeholder host would make the dead-entry assertion permanently red, and the honest statement is that there is nothing to extract.

## The disclosure half

`scripts/check-landing-drift.mjs` already owned "did the copy stop matching the code" — its check 5 parses the `SCRAPERS` registry out of Rust to gate landing claims. Three checks join it: every publicly-named third party in the inventory must appear as a **whole word** on the real disclosure surfaces; the over-absolute claim shape ADR-0005 exists because of is banned; the vendored chart.js hash is pinned.

## Documentation that was wrong

- The privacy page said *"the only network calls are the AI-provider and job-board requests described above, which you trigger"* — omitting Exa, Photon, Clearbit and IMAP, and wrong about Sentry, which ADR-0020 made default **ON**. Both README and SECURITY carried the same shape.
- The updater was described as *"an on-launch check"*. `updater/mod.rs`'s own doc comment says *"Silent check 10 s after launch, then every 4 h"* — the app's only always-on, untoggleable egress.
- ADR-0005 still claimed README and SECURITY *"must be rewritten … not yet applied"* long after they were, and pointed class 8 at a file containing no Sentry code.
- 28 broken ADR links, dead since #1000 merged the two ADR trees.

## Review

title: fix: generate the résumé in the job ad's language, and notice when it doesn't
body:
A German job ad produced an **English résumé with German headings**, alongside a correctly German cover letter. Pressing Regenerate produced a German résumé. Three separate defects sit behind that, and the load-bearing one is that nothing in the app noticed.

## What the diagnostics log proved

```
[validate:content] → kind=resume lang=de        ← the target WAS German, both runs
[validate:content] ← kind=resume lang=de issues=10 criticals=0 ok=true
[pipeline:resume_quality] → stage=repair … duration=0ms   ← nothing to repair
```

That `lang=` is `normalize_language(input.target_language)` — the target, not the detected language. Corroborated independently: the shipped PDF carries *Profil* / *Berufserfahrung*, which can only come from `resume_conventions("de")`, and export does not localize headings.

So the run asked for German both times. Both runs took the same code path and resolved the same language. ADR-032 already claimed the invariant — it lists "language misalignment" among the deterministic Criticals Rust withdraws from the model. The guarantee was documented and not delivered.

## Root cause

**The draft prompt never asked the model to translate.** `draft_system` said only *"…in de"* — a bare two-letter code — while everything around it pulled toward the source: `FACTUAL_GROUNDING_RULES`, the "exactly as given" clause, English strategy artifacts, and an English source résumé. The TS prompt this was ported from carries the translate rule twice. The model did the only consistent thing: it translated the four heading strings it was handed and copied the body. The letter obeyed because its prompt injects real German (`Betreff`, market conventions, a German date format) and has no source document to preserve.

**Both language guards were dead in exactly the cross-language case.** `source_is_a_reliable_control` required the SOURCE résumé to already read as the target — true only when no translation is needed. English source + German target disabled the document-level Critical *and* the per-section drift pass. The cover letter was unchecked the same way.

**The identity question was routed through a stemmer predicate.** `languages_align` answers "should both sides use the same Snowball algorithm". Twelve non-Latin languages return `false` against their own locale, and every non-Snowball Latin language aligns only with `en`. Repairing only the control would have unmasked false Criticals across ~19 languages.

Plus two adjacent defects: the persisted-language branch from #1003 read fields the pipeline never writes, and the AI-Generate path seeded the target from the **source résumé's** language — pinning an English résumé to English regardless of the ad.

## The fix

- `documents::keywords::detected_language()` answers language **identity**, separate from `languages_align`'s stemmer question, sharing one tag table so the two cannot drift. Reliability delegates to whatlang's own `Info::is_reliable()`.
- `target_is_corroborated` replaces the broken control: the job ad **or** the source must confidently read as the target. Applied to both the document-level and per-section passes.
- `draft_system` gained an explicit translate rule; every SYSTEM prompt now names the language ("in German", not "in de") via a closed Rust-owned table, so the ADR-010 surface is *narrower* than before. Job titles deliberately stay untranslated — `consistency.title_drift` would otherwise fire on every cross-language run.
- One automatic draft retry, bounded structurally (two straight-line calls, no loop, no flag, in a stage constructed fresh per run). It keeps the second attempt only if it fixed the language, and does not stream, so the live pane never renders the document twice.
- `criticals_by_section` no longer mis-routes a document-wide language Critical. Its evidence was a two-character code and `sections::containing` is a raw substring search — `"de"` matched *der*/*Kunden* — so a whole-document failure burned repair attempts on an arbitrary section.
- The renderer resolves the target from the job ad, never the source résumé, and a guessed language is used for the current run but never persisted — on every write path, not just `session.start`.

`validate/content/mod.rs` was at exactly the R8 1400-line cap, so the language family moved to `validate/content/language.rs` in a separate pure-move commit.

## Known open issue — please read before merging

**A truthful English résumé in terse noun-phrase register can earn a false language Critical.** `whatlang`'s `confidence()` is a top-1-vs-top-2 margin, not a probability, so a `-tion`/`-ment`-dense finance or consulting CV reads as French at **1.0000**. `target_is_corroborated` then believes the job ad, and a correct document is flagged — which sets `language_mismatch`, making `posting_comparable()` false and blanking `keyword_coverage` and every alignment finding.

It also costs money: `Draft::run` gates the retry on the same predicate, so an affected run fires a second full draft and discards it. Roughly 2× draft spend, deterministic per input class.

Reproduced and measured against the pinned whatlang. A second reviewer could not reproduce it with three of its own English fixtures (`Eng` at 0.23 / 0.85 / 0.93), so the triggering register is narrow — but it is real and it is a regression against `main`, which was silent here.

No fix is agreed yet — swapping in a different detector for the identity question was considered and rejected. Two approaches are already falsified by measurement: requiring the output to read as the source language (a same-length, same-register source also reads French at 1.0000), and token overlap with the source (high in both the true and the false positive). Tracked as a follow-up.

Also worth knowing: two different detectors decide and check this question — franc picks the target renderer-side, whatlang checks the output in Rust. Corroboration fails quiet when they disagree; reading the generated document fails loud. That asymmetry is documented in ADR-032 and `matching-algorithm.md`.

`validate::content` is never called from `export/` (ADR-034), so a surviving Critical parks the run at `needsReview` but does not gate export. Unchanged here.

## Review

A security gate plus a three-pass ensemble ran before this went up. The gate found no HIGH/CRITICAL. The ensemble blocked twice and both were real:

- **`section_language_issues` fired without corroboration** — the section pass kept the paradox-avoidance guard but lost the corroboration requirement, reopening the same false-Critical class at section scope. Worse, the obvious regression test for the fix would have been vacuous: `EN_WRONG_LANGUAGE` reads German at 1.0000, so the second condition already closes the gate. The committed test uses a measured discriminating fixture (whole document `Eng` @ 0.2833 → unreliable, `EXPERIENCE` section `Ita` @ 1.0) and was mutation-checked in both directions.
- **The guessed language leaked into the saved aggregate** via two sibling save paths, re-creating the English lock one door over.

Review also found a pre-existing test that never tested anything — a certifications guard whose fixture had a lowercase-word ratio of 0.0, so `looks_like_prose` filtered it before the language comparison was ever reached.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check` clean · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` clean · `cargo test --all-features --locked` → **4155 lib + 18 architecture + 3 eval**, 0 failed · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `eslint --max-warnings 0` on every changed TS file clean · `gen:prompts:check` up to date · renderer suites 631 passed.

Every new guard carries a mutation check that was actually run and observed red, not asserted in a comment.

title: fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, and keep the regenerate language
body:
Fixes three user-reported generation defects, then the architectural cause behind them, then everything a security gate and a four-pass review found in the fixes.

## The three reported bugs

**A résumé came out with its summary in English, work experience in Italian, and skills in English again.** `content.language_mismatch` read the whole document, and `languages_align` returns the *dominant* language — so a majority vote hid exactly this. Measured: one drifted section undetected, two undetected, three detected.

**Empty `Projects` / `Publications` sections appeared with nothing in them.** My own regression from #998: the draft prompt said *"Order the sections EXACTLY as: … do not reorder, **drop**, or invent"*, which reads as a nine-item manifest plus a ban on omitting anything. The model did as it was told.

**Regenerate re-generated in English, discarding the job ad's language.** `useTailorPipeline` re-detected from `jobDesc` on every render and treated "I can't tell" as "it's English" — while the run's own persisted `resumeLanguage` sat unread forty lines below.

## Why all three happened at once

PRs #969/#992 moved generation from **one whole-document model call** to **per-section calls that cannot see their siblings**. Before that, coherence was free. After it, each section is written by a call with no idea what the others say, and the guarantee was replaced by a prompt instruction. Instructions drift.

The validator was written two days before that change, for whole-document output. Its majority-vote language check was *correct for that world*.

## What an audit of the same seam found

Measured, not argued — one CRITICAL and four HIGH:

- **A repair round could silently delete a job.** The guard searched the *whole document* for the employer, so a Summary sentence naming it spared the deletion of its entire Experience entry. `roles 2→1`, round accepted, document persisted.
- **A reply containing the whole document was accepted** and spliced over one section — 6 sections → 10, and the exported PDF showed four sections twice. Under mutation it compounded to 4×.
- **A reply for a *different* section was accepted** — ask for Summary, receive Skills, and the Summary is destroyed.
- **`round_is_worse` couldn't see any of it**, while its sibling `humanize_is_worse` guarded coverage and voice — and repair runs *first*, makes up to eight blind rewrites, and had the weaker rule.

## What review then found in the fixes

A security gate (clean on security; one HIGH correctness), a three-pass ensemble, and a confirmation pass. Highlights:

- **The Rust suite was red and I reported it green.** `cargo test --lib` doesn't build `tests/eval.rs`; CI's `nextest --all-features` does. The repo's corpus guard was working perfectly — a fixture graded by nothing — and I ran a command too narrow to hear it.
- **`project_link_issues` accused users of inventing their own links.** Widened on the generated side only, so a résumé with both `PROJECTS` and `SIDE PROJECTS` flagged its own link — unclearably, since repair routes the finding to the *first* Projects section.
- **A fix that scoped a search by section kind turned "absent" into "deleted"**, so a truthful résumé headed `Work History` earned two unclearable Criticals.
- **The splice gate had no test.** Both guard tests rebuilt the check in their own closure, so deleting a clause from production left all 137 green — while a docstring claimed the mutation was verified.

## The pattern underneath all of it

Every defect here — the original three, the audit's five, and the ones my own fixes introduced — is the same error: **substituting a proxy for the property you actually care about.**

| proxy | actual property |
| --- | --- |
| whole-document search | did this entry survive |
| a heading list | is this the experience section |
| text-emptiness | is this section absent |
| a `SectionKind` allowlist | is this section prose |
| two cargo commands | do the tests pass |

Each proxy is right in the common case and wrong in precisely the case the check exists to catch.

## Also in here

The **skills section had no specified shape** — `resume_conventions.skills` is only the localised heading, so the model chose, and the repo's own fixtures disagree. Now grouped inline lists, one line per group, with the bullet form explicitly prohibited rather than merely undescribed. A bullet per skill spends a line on one word; an ATS extracts a comma list just as well.

Each section-rewrite call now also receives a **fenced anchor of the surrounding document** (Summary + one representative bullet) so it can match the language, voice and tense already on the page — the coherence one-shot generation had implicitly. Security-reviewed: registration proven load-bearing by mutation (sibling-forgery count 1→5), neutralization is a fixed point, no new egress.

## Known and deliberate

Drift confined to a `Skills` section is detected but not prevented by the anchor. `looks_like_prose` skips an all-lowercase list by design — the `Skills` exclusion carries that class. The whole-document fallback in `generated_experience_lower` accepts a possible miss over a guaranteed false Critical.

`commands/resume_pipeline/mod.rs` and `export/typst_engine/letter.rs` sit at the R8 1400-LOC cap; neither is touched here, but the next change to either needs a split first.

## Verification

`cargo test --all-features --locked` — **4124 lib + 18 architecture + 3 eval** · clippy `-D warnings` clean · fmt clean · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `pnpm test` 478 files / 6903 tests.

Every guard mutation-checked — broken, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green — independently by me as well as by the authoring agents. Commits are kept separate so the validator-semantics layer can be reverted without losing the reported-bug fixes.

title: docs: make adr-034's placeholder note a thin pointer
body:
Follow-up to #998, addressing the one review finding that was still open when that PR merged.

ADR-034's Consequence #2 update restated the placeholder predicate's matching rules (bracket syntax, en/de tokens, case-insensitivity, punctuation tolerance) and the validation call path, against the knowledge base's own rule that docs are thin pointers into the owning symbol with no copied literals.

It had already begun to drift, in the same PR that wrote it: the text still named `locale::letter::is_template_placeholder` after #998 moved the symbol to the module root.

## What was cut

The defect narrative, the predicate's matching rules, and the parser mechanics. Those belong with `locale::is_template_placeholder`, `parse_cover_letter`, and `validate::content::letter`.

## What was kept, deliberately

Two things that are contract rather than mechanics, and are not derivable from reading a symbol:

- **`validate::content` is never called from `export/`.** The export path calls `validate::validate_and_fix`, a structural PDF/DOCX round-trip checker. So `letter.template_placeholder` does **not** block an export — the parser filter is what stops bad bytes reaching rendered output. An earlier draft of this ADR claimed the opposite and had to be corrected once already.
- **Only the placeholder shape of drift is closed.** Other unanticipated furniture shapes are still caught only by human review.

## Note on style

The symbol references are bare backtick paths rather than markdown links. All 34 sibling ADRs use that form and this file's own Related section already did, so linking would have made the file internally inconsistent — fixing a consistency finding by introducing a different inconsistency.

Docs only; no source files touched.

title: docs: fold the second adr tree into the knowledge base
body:
The repo had **two ADR directories with colliding numbers**. `docs/adr/0013` is email watching; `adr-013` is the resume builder. Both get cited as "ADR-13", and it has already caused a wrong citation.

## Which one is canonical

`docs/knowledge/decision-records/` — created 2026-05-31 with the knowledge base, indexed in its README, owned by `project-steward`, and the only one the `docs-standards` skill points at.

`docs/adr/` appeared **twelve days later** (2026-06-12), carried no index and no owner, and nothing in the repo's rules referenced it. It grew to 23 records because nothing stopped it.

## Moved, deliberately not renumbered

An ADR is a dated record, and its number is an identifier other things point at — commit messages, merged PR bodies, code comments, and the published tech radar. `apps/landing/public/benchmarks/data.js` and `metrics/*.json` are **generated captures of commit text** containing strings like `ADR-0021` and `ADR 0005`.

Renumbering would falsify all of it, so the `NNNN-` series is folded in as-is and marked **closed** in the index: cite existing ones by their current numbers, give every new ADR the next `adr-NNN`. This is standard ADR practice — supersede, never renumber.

Git tracked all 23 as renames, so `git log --follow` still works.

## What follows the move

- 24 live files updated, including the tech radar's `ADR_DIR` and its **public GitHub blob links** (those would otherwise 404)
- Relative links *inside* the moved files gained a directory level; each was verified to resolve
- `docs/knowledge/README.md` now indexes all **57** ADRs, with the closed series and the reasoning recorded
- Generated snapshots under `apps/landing/public/` deliberately left untouched as the historical records they are

## Reviewer note — a user-visible consequence

This changes **published URLs**. Anyone holding a bookmarked `docs/adr/...` link will 404, and GitHub does not redirect moved paths. They would have broken on any move; calling it out rather than burying it.

## Verification

`check:tech-radar` (40 entries, every `adrSlug` resolves) · `check:agent-system` (which explicitly validates the ADR index) · `check:landing-drift` · typecheck · lint · prettier · full TS suite **478 files / 6898 tests**.

The pre-push gate caught one real breakage: `check-tech-radar.test.mjs` writes its fixture ADR via `join(repoDir, 'docs', 'adr', …)`. A path assembled from segments is invisible to a `docs/adr/` grep, so the reference sweep missed it. Fixture repointed; assertions unchanged.

title: feat(scraping): treat an implausible scraped company name as absent
body:
Closes A1 from the hardening plan — the root cause behind #960, where six generated cover letters carried garbage company names because the scraper returned things like `"Apply now | LinkedIn"` as the employer.

## Why nothing caught it

Every existing guard passed, and correctly. `validate/content/factual.rs` checks generated text **against the job ad**, so faithfully reproducing a garbage company is not a factual error. The hole was upstream of every validator: nothing ever asked whether the ingested posting was sane.

## The fix

`is_implausible_company` + `TrustFlag::ImplausibleCompany` in `scraping::trust`. That module's contract is *"V1 is flag-only: enrich, never drop"*, so it gains signal and blocks nothing.

Acting on it happens at two real boundaries rather than by blocking:

- `commands/resume_pipeline` blanks an implausible company before it can seed company research or the persisted record
- `export/commands::generate_filename` falls back to the same default an absent name already gets

Passing `None` rather than garbage lets the **existing** prompt contract take over — it already says to name only the role when no company is provided — so no prompt text changed.

## A correction to the premise

The task was scoped from #960's postmortem, which describes a letter addressed to the garbage company. **That symptom no longer exists.** Since #997, `complete_letter_text` always inserts a generic salutation regardless of company, so the addressee line is already safe (verified in `export/letter_shape.rs`).

What still leaked is subtler: the garbage company **seeds the company-research web search**, so the "why this company" paragraph is researched against nonsense, and it **persists into the exported record and filename**. Those are the boundaries guarded here. A postmortem describes the bug when it was found, not the code today.

## What review changed

The first pass shipped the failure mode that matters more than the bug — **it rejected real employers**. Confirmed by executing the predicate:

| | before review | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Monster Worldwide` | rejected | accepted |
| `Xing SE` | rejected | accepted |
| `Indeed Inc` | rejected | accepted |
| `Glassdoor Inc` | rejected | accepted |
| `Apply On Demand Inc` | rejected | accepted |
| `LinkedIn` | rejected | rejected |
| `Apply now` | rejected | rejected |
| `Apply now \| LinkedIn` | rejected | rejected |

All five are real companies that hire directly and post under their own names. A false positive silently deletes a real employer from a user's letter, which is worse than the original defect.

Both offending rules matched too loosely: `JOB_BOARD_NAMES` rejected any name *containing* a board token as a word, and `CTA_PHRASES` substring-matched. Both now match only when the **entire normalized name is** the board name or CTA phrase. The originally-reported string is still rejected — by the separator rule, not by either loosened list — and a test pins that so the coverage cannot be accidental. `"Apply on Indeed"` becomes an accepted false negative, pinned as a deliberate choice rather than left to be rediscovered.

## A guard that was blind by construction

The new enum variant serialises as `implausibleCompany`, but the hand-maintained TS union and both locale files still listed four flags, while `TrustBadge` calls `t(...)` unconditionally. The badge would have rendered the literal key `jobs.trust.flags.implausibleCompany` — in both languages, on exactly the postings this branch exists to fix.

The repo's purpose-built *"i18n key-drift guard"* test stayed green through all of it, because its fixture list derives from the same stale union it is meant to guard. A guard sourced from the thing it guards is not a guard.

Fixed structurally rather than by adding a case: an exhaustive `Record<TrustFlag, string>` now lives in **production** code, so a future missing variant fails `pnpm typecheck` for the whole app, not one test file. Mutation-checked in both directions.

## Known, deliberate

A bare single character is rejected, which rejects the real company `X`. At that length truncation overwhelmingly dominates, and the cost of being wrong is soft — the letter names the role instead. Flagging it rather than burying it.

`commands/resume_pipeline/mod.rs` sits at 1398/1400 LOC (R8 hard cap). Not a violation; anything further there needs code moved out first.

## Verification

`cargo test --lib` 4092/0 · `cargo test --test architecture` 18/18 · clippy `-D warnings` clean · fmt clean · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm test` 478 files / 6899 tests.

Every guard mutation-checked — broken, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green — including independently by me rather than only by the authoring agent. Neutering the predicate kills four tests across three layers.

title: fix(export): restore lost bold, kill the letter placeholder, and make section order deterministic
body:
Fixes a run of résumé and cover-letter defects found by rendering all 16 résumé templates and all 6 letter layouts and looking at them. Several turned out to be data loss rather than styling.

## The bugs

**Bold never rendered in a résumé bullet — in any template, in either backend.** `parse_line` strips markdown into `clean` up front, then the bullet arm matched `BULLET_RE` against `clean` instead of `trimmed`, so the captured text had already lost its `**` markers before `tokenize_rich` saw it. It emitted `bold: false` every time. The two-space-gap `JobEntry` arm had the same defect, and `adapter.rs` compounded it by tokenizing `line.text` (stripped) instead of `line.raw`. Every other `parse_line` arm was audited and was already correct.

This mattered beyond appearance: generation deliberately emphasises keywords with `**`, so every tailored résumé was silently losing that emphasis on the way to the page. Measured before/after on the same fixture: **0 → 4** bold runs.

**Every German cover letter rendered an unfilled template placeholder as the candidate's job title.** The model reproduces a letter template's `Ihr Name` slot verbatim; `parse_cover_letter`'s post-signoff rule ("first non-blank non-name line becomes `signature_title`") promoted it. `complete_letter_text` did not intervene either — its idempotency guard only checks that a salutation *and* a sign-off are present, not that what sits between them is real content. This is the drift ADR-034 Consequence #2 recorded as unguarded. Now closed by a shared `is_template_placeholder` predicate plus a Critical `letter.template_placeholder` issue.

**Résumé section order was an LLM free choice, re-rolled every generation.** `ResumeStrategy.section_order` was a free-form `Vec<String>` (schema: array of arbitrary strings, no enum), the draft prompt said only "follow its section order", and no Rust code ever read the field. Meanwhile the ATS-correct order lived in a market-blind const that only applied in ATS mode. Replaced with `locale::resume::section_order_for(market)` as one source read by both the prompt and `linearize`; `sectionOrder` is gone from the schema.

**Education entry titles rendered unbolded everywhere except the Academic template**, because `emphasize_education` was `t.id == TemplateId::Academic`. This also closes a real PDF/DOCX divergence: `RunOpts::entry_title` already forced bold unconditionally, so DOCX had been bolding education all along while PDF had not — contradicting the golden-parity claim in adr-002.

## Spacing, fixed centrally

Every one of these was the same shape: a shared token existed and templates bypassed it with literals.

| Gap | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry title → subtitle (role, degree) | `sp-subtitle-gap` 1pt | 6pt |
| Name → contact | hardcoded in 8 templates at 3/4/5/6/9pt | all route through `sp-name-below` |
| Name → header role | hardcoded 2pt in meridian + awesome | `sp-subtitle-gap` |
| Letter sign-off / name / role | six per-layout literals (20–34pt) | two shared tokens, one unbreakable block |

Grouping the letter signature also means a page break can no longer separate a name from its sign-off.

`letter_refined` and `letter_sidebar` now stack contact entries vertically — a long contact line was claiming enough of the header grid's `auto` column to wrap the candidate's name onto two lines.

A markdown link whose label is the bare URL now renders through `url_label`, so a contact reads "LinkedIn" rather than the full href as body text.

## Notes for review

Awesome's header band is content-measured, so widening a header gap overflows its floor. `band-min-h` has now been bumped twice by this PR (28 → 29 → 31mm). Its doc comment records both bumps and names the test that catches it — treat that constant as coupled to header spacing, not as a settled value.

`export/typst_engine/letter.rs` sits at exactly the R8 1400-LOC cap. It passes, but the next change to that file will fail CI; it wants splitting.

## Known gap, not addressed here

`SectionId::from_header` matches English keywords only. A genuinely German résumé (`BERUFSERFAHRUNG`, `AUSBILDUNG`, `KENNTNISSE`) classifies all 13 sections as `Custom`, so the DE section order added here does not apply to it. Verified empirically. The English-only classifier predates this work and its source comment already noted the localised-headings phase was never built — worth a follow-up.

## Verification

Every fix was mutation-checked: the guard was broken, the test confirmed red, then restored. That caught two tests passing for the wrong reason — one whose fixture fell through the parser's `JobEntry` shape rule so both renders were identical regardless of the fix, and a market-awareness test that compared two identical strings after the default order changed.

All 23 templates were rendered to PDF and reviewed visually against a full fixture exercising 13 section kinds, bold runs, inline links, a five-part contact line and wrapping bullets.

`cargo test --lib` 4078 passed / 0 failed · `cargo test --test architecture` 18/18 · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` clean.

Also adds a "Licensing and contributions" section to CONTRIBUTING.md: the file said nothing about licensing, so a prospective contributor had no way to tell what rights they were granting by opening a PR.

title: fix: complete the cover letter at the export boundary and repair the pipeline regressions
body:
## The bug

The staged pipeline's letter prompt (`pipeline/resume/prompts.rs`, `letter_system`) tells the model:

> Do NOT write a contact header, a salutation line, or a signature block — **the application adds them at export time**.

The application never did. `parse_cover_letter` only ever *parsed* those parts out of a full letter. The résumé side of the identical promise **is** kept (`validate/mod.rs`, `ContactProfile::apply_to_header`), which is why résumés looked right and letters did not.

Introduced by `19a6de3e` (apply flow → staged pipeline), which deleted the one-shot TS path along with `extractMetadata`, the full-letter prompt, the market-conventions block and company research. Not by the agentic deletion in `93174a1c` — that prompt actually produced complete letters.

### What a real German letter rendered as

| Slot | Should be | Rendered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `letterhead.name` | the candidate | the whole 380-char opening paragraph |
| `date` | 16. August 2026 | a body paragraph containing "0 % auf 90 %." |
| `body` | 3–5 rich paragraphs | **empty** |
| `salutation` / `signoff` | market pair | **absent** |
| `signature_name` | the candidate | the opening paragraph, again |

With no salutation the parser never starts the body, so every paragraph fell into the pre-salutation branch and rendered as recipient lines: plain text, hard line breaks, no bold, no paragraph spacing.

## The fix

`complete_letter_text` synthesises the market salutation, sign-off and signature name for a body-only letter, inserted **after** any leading subject/date furniture. It is called once from `validate_and_normalize`, so PDF, both DOCX scanners and the live preview all inherit it — and **every letter already stored renders correctly with no regeneration**. Verified idempotent, so a full letter still round-trips byte-identically.

Also in scope, because the same cutover caused them:

- **Market etiquette** — `<market_conventions>`, the subject line and an app-supplied date are back in the prompt; the market is resolved from the posting's location, so US postings get US Letter instead of A4.
- **Bold** — the prompts ask for keyword emphasis again (letter *and* résumé draft); `sanitize_markdown` already preserves `**…**`.
- **ATS/quality panel** — `top_requirements` now comes from the `analyze_job` stage rather than the request the tailor surface sends empty. That single change un-starves the requirement metric, stops the empty list freezing the keyword chips through a pick-non-empty merge, and makes `regenerate_section` validate against the same list the run used. The renderer's `meta` is seeded from the aggregate instead of fabricated, which also stops a non-null stub short-circuiting the answers assistant's own extraction.
- **`humanize`** ran after validation with gates that never looked at keyword coverage; it now rejects a rewrite that drops coverage past the existing threshold.
- **Company research** reaches the letter again, opt-in, through the *same* `AI_RESEARCH_BUCKET` rate/concurrency limiter and provider daily ceiling as the existing command — one named constant, one runtime bucket, guard held across the call.
- Predicate hardening: a name is capped at 64 chars / 8 tokens, a date at 48 / 8; the letterhead name falls back to the contact profile before the letter's first line.

## Guardrails

Every existing letter test fed a *complete* letter — the shape the **old** prompt produced. That is exactly why this survived. Added adversarial body-only fixtures carrying the three traps from the real incident (long opening paragraph, digits-and-period paragraph, a bold keyword) plus PDF text-layer and DOCX `document.xml` contract tests, **verified failing** against a neutered `complete_letter_text`. A prompt↔export lock test names the synthesiser that must be retired if the prompt ever stops delegating.

## Verification

`cargo test --lib` 4051 passed · `cargo test --test architecture` 18 · clippy `--all-features -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` clean · `pnpm test` 6898 passed / 478 files · typecheck 13/13 · `lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean · `gen:ipc:check` in sync.

Security review found no HIGH/CRITICAL. Its MEDIUM findings are fixed here: a third export path (`GenerationCard`) still sent no locale and would have appended an English salutation to a German letter — a defect this branch introduced — and the new fence assertions were vacuous until the hostile payload was extended to forge the tags it asserts on (mutation-tested red, then green).

## Known gaps, recorded not fixed

Pipeline letters still lose link injection (TS-side, needs porting); tone/mode/applicant-preference conditioning is still absent from the staged letter prompt. The Jobs-page match badge is a cached score of the *saved default* résumé and no surface has ever re-scored it after a generation — making it move is a product decision, not a regression fix.

ADR-034 records the ownership split.

title: fix: pipeline timeouts, fence leaks, the generation-application fk, and rust edition 2024
body:
Four independently-developed fix branches folded into one PR (55 files, well under the split threshold), plus the findings from the pre-PR review ensemble.

## 1. Timeout reporting — a run that looked stuck for 7 minutes

A local run parked on **Analyze** with no explanation and finished with `stopped=-`.

- `strategy` hit exactly `300_013 ms`. `STREAM_BASELINE_SECS` is effort-scaled, but the non-streaming `OLLAMA_COMPLETION` baseline was flat — and `analyze_job`, `match_evidence` and `strategy` are *all* non-streaming, so the three slowest-on-local stages had a cap that raising the effort could not lift. The completion deadline now scales by effort too.
- `StoppedReason::Timeout` existed in the enum with **no producer**, and the renderer's `STOPPED_SUFFIX` deliberately omitted it. A per-call timeout now produces the reason and a message, and the UI renders it.
- The timeout banner carries `{ kind, stage, seconds }` as structured data and is localized through `pipeline.timeout` + the existing `pipeline.stage.*` labels, instead of hardcoded English with a raw internal stage key.
- `effort` joined the stage cache key — it reaches Ollama as `think`, so it changes the output and could not stay out of the key.
- One `map_completion_transport_error` helper replaces the same timeout/network classification copy-pasted across four provider adapters. The timeout branch never interpolates the error's `Display` (no URL or secret leak).

## 2. `<humanize_document>` tags in the exported PDF

The humanize prompt's own wrapper was echoed back by the model, accepted, saved as the résumé, and exported.

`is_usable_rewrite` only checked emptiness and a length ratio — and a wrapper *adds* length, so it passed. Every acceptance check asked "is this good writing?"; none asked "is this still a document?" Humanize and repair now reject any candidate carrying a registered prompt-fence tag (revert to the original, never strip), and the save path refuses a document that echoes one.

The save gate reads `ctx.letter` — what is actually persisted — not `letter_text()`, whose fallback is the user's own pasted reference letter. Gating on the fallback meant a tag in text this run never generates and never stores would discard the **entire** save, clean résumé included, after a multi-minute run.

## 3. Cover letter generated but never shown; the résumé appeared in both tabs

`persist_document` never set `application_id` on the `ai_generations` row, and the renderer filters by it — so the letter was generated (1682 chars), validated three times, and then invisible.

The same NULL FK silently broke `applications_delete(keep_documents = false)`: it matched zero rows, so "delete this application and its documents" left the documents behind. A backfill that matches zero rows looks exactly like success, which is why this went unnoticed.

- `persist_document` now establishes the link on save — **read-only** (`find_by_job_url`), never create-on-miss.
- `link_orphaned_generations` runs at store open, before the wider backfill, and only ever *links*.
- The wide backfill may only CREATE for rows provably older than `APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS` (2026-06-11), so a deleted application cannot be resurrected on the next app start.

## 4. Elapsed timer reset to 0 on navigate-away-and-back

Anchored on the backend run's own `startedAt` rather than component mount, guarded against `0` and clock skew, and relabelled "{{time}} total".

## 5. Rust edition 2024

`edition = "2024"`, `rust-version = "1.95"`, toolchain pinned to `1.97.1`. The crate has zero `unsafe fn` and zero `static mut`, so the migration was nearly free — the one behavioural change is `if_let_rescope`, which alters when a temporary lock guard drops. That is silent, so the deferrals are documented in the crate. `rustfmt.toml` pins `style_edition = "2021"`; unpinning it reformats ~200 files in 374 hunks and belongs in its own commit, not hidden inside this one.

## Also

- The per-stage models card no longer describes the depth setting that was deleted with the agentic surfaces (en + de).
- Timeout-baseline tests were welded to `STREAM_BASELINE_SECS` while asserting completion behaviour — they now pin the constant they actually describe, and were mutation-tested to prove they still fail on a real divergence.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` · `cargo test --workspace` (4004 lib + 18 architecture + 3 eval) · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm gen:ipc:check` · `pnpm test` 478 files / 6868 tests.

Every new test in this batch was mutation-tested — reverted the fix, confirmed the test reddens, restored. Six tests earlier in this session turned out to be unable to fail for what they claimed, which is why that step is now non-optional.

  * Generation timing now persists across stage changes and reconnects.

  * Runs stopped by timeout remain visible in run history.
  * Added migration and restore support for linking eligible legacy generations to applications.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevented prompt-fence artifacts from being saved in résumés or cover letters.

title: feat: delete the agentic surfaces and extract the prompt fencing
body:
Deletes the agentic surfaces — the "Prep this application" flow and `improve_resume` — after first extracting the prompt-injection fencing that lived inside them. **98 files, +1,113 / −19,013.** Last of five PRs in the multi-stage pipeline programme, after #990, #991, #992 and #993.

## Why

The owner ruled the agentic machinery was spending tokens without producing anything worth keeping. The **browser extension's answer-assist stays** — that is the one agent-adjacent capability deliberately kept.

## Extraction first, deletion second

`agent/` could not simply be deleted: a large amount of ADR-010 fencing machinery lived inside it and is used by code that survives — the staged résumé pipeline (`pipeline/resume/prompts.rs`), which fences scraped job postings and prior-stage model output, and the extension's answer-assist.

So step 1 moved `fenced`, the caps, `neutralize_transcript_boundaries`, `FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS` and its neutralization functions into a new dependency-free `prompt_fence` module (L0), and re-pointed every consumer. The security review confirmed the move was faithful at the byte level: a comment-stripped diff of the moved region yields exactly one hunk (the three items deliberately left behind), and all 16 moved tests are byte-identical — including the two subtlest bits, the attribute-form pattern and the inner-`<` breaker.

Steps 2–4 then deleted `agent/`, `commands/agent.rs`, the renderer surfaces (`PrepApplicationPanel`, `AgentConfirm`, `ImproveResumeRun`, `useAgentRunSession`, `services/use-agent/`, `agent-run.machine`, and `TailoredResumePanel`), and the IPC contract layer.

## The finding that justifies the review cost

`FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS` is an allowlist where a **missing entry is a prompt-injection hole**. The security reviewer removed each of the 24 entries individually and ran the suite after each: **15 could be deleted with all 3,968 tests green — 10 of them tags surviving code still emits.** Only 9 were guarded at all.

That is not theoretical. A docs agent trimmed three entries from this list earlier the same day while "fixing a comment"; it was caught by a human, not by CI.

The subtlety that made it invisible: `every_untrusted_block_is_fenced_and_forgery_resistant` *does* assert on `</job_analysis>`, but its hostile payload only ever forges `</job_posting>` — so that entry was inert to the assertion. Moving a test set verbatim proves the tests did not weaken; it proves nothing about entries no test forges.

Now closed by a table-driven test. Note it does **not** simply iterate the live registry — that cannot catch its own deletions, since removing an entry just means the loop tests one fewer thing and passes. It pairs the loop with an independent hardcoded list and a set-equality check, so a deletion fails the equality check and a weakening fails the loop.

## Also from review

- **Extension fence coverage** went from 1 of 6 untrusted blocks to all 6, including the two with the strongest attacker story (`company_research`, `web_search_notes` — both web-sourced). Behaviour was already correct; the coverage was not. Breaking `fenced` now reddens the pipeline and the extension **separately**, rather than both relying on one distant test.
- **Three more orphans**, found by a better method than delete-and-compile-one-at-a-time: temporarily make every module private, compile, and diff the unused-item set against the same run at the merge base. `report::for_saved_resume`, `report::agent_save_pipeline`, and `PipelineRunStore::update_status_if_present` — the last of which delete-and-compile missed because its own tests still referenced it.
- **`prompt_fence` is now genuinely L0.** `RESUME_CAP` was imported from generated code, forcing an architecture exception spanning L0→L3 — and that constant had no TS consumer left. It is a local literal now, which cleared the exception, `packages/shared/src/agent-caps.ts`, and its codegen target.
- **The error-echo clamp** in `resolve.rs` lost its only guard when `commands/agent.rs` was deleted; replacing its body with a no-op left all tests green. Now asserted.

## Verified, not assumed

The architecture review confirmed the deletion changed no surviving behaviour: `AUTOPILOT_NOTE_SYSTEM` relocated byte-identical, `limits::AGENT_RUN_*` values unchanged (now single-consumer), the `StoppedReason` wire contract intact, no migration or data-store schema touched, and en/de translations symmetric at −164 each. `Budget::RESUME_QUALITY` compared field-by-field against base: identical.

It also confirmed the provider tool-calling surface (`AiProvider::chat_with_tools`, `ToolSpec`, `AgentTurn` and five implementations) is now genuinely unreachable — **flagged, not deleted**, since it belongs to the AI-provider domain. Important for whoever acts on it: `ChatMsg`, `flatten_messages`, `Usage` and `StopReason` are still live, and the removal is code *plus* tests.

## Rider

`fix/reset-stale-refs` is folded in — a one-file renderer fix, file-disjoint from the deletion. `reset()` cleared state but left three refs stale until React committed, so a late event for the just-reset run could overwrite the new session's stage and error text. The state machine already protected the coarse status field, so the symptom was a reset screen flashing the previous run's progress. Mutation-verified.

## Testing

`cargo test --workspace` 3,970 passed · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` · `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check` · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm test` 478 files / 6,855 tests · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0`.

## Summary

PR-1 of the apply-flow pipeline programme (analyze → generate → validate → remove AI signs). Makes the Projects section **code-owned at quality depth** — the format guarantee that previously existed only in max depth's assemble stage — and preserves markdown link labels (`[Website](url)` / `[Github](url)`) from the source résumé through seeding, rendering, and export.

- New pure L2 module `pipeline/resume/projects.rs`: `normalize_projects` re-renders the draft's Projects section from source-seeded `ProjectOut` entries via the existing 3-tier ladder (`render_project`), preserving the model's project order, restoring altered/dropped links, and keeping labeled link spans byte-verbatim.
- **Narrow write authority**: only entries positively matched to a seed are rewritten; unmatched draft entries stay verbatim for the validators to grade. Five structural whole-bail guards (`no_entry_starts`, `empty_seed`, `implausible_seeds`, `draft_parse_disagreement`, `link_in_description`) turn the pass off — with a content-free `projectsNormalizeSkipped` ledger reason — whenever the seeds show any signature of mis-grouping (plain-text extractions, achievement-bullet phantom entries, swallowed title lines).
- Hooks: after the draft stage, inside `repair_loop` (before revalidate), and on Projects-scoped `regenerate_section` (real-provenance sources only).

title: feat(apply): the apply flow runs the staged 4-step pipeline on both surfaces
body:
The apply flow now runs the staged quality pipeline instead of the one-shot fast path, and shows it as four visible steps — **Analyze → Generate → Validate → Remove AI signs** — identically from the Jobs page and from an Autopilot found-job apply. Third of five PRs in the multi-stage pipeline programme (after #990 projects normalization and #991 cover-letter + humanize stages).

## Why the apply flow couldn't run staged before

The run request could only resolve a job ad server-side out of the Jobs-page postings cache, so anything pasted or autopilot-sourced had no `jobId` and fell back to the one-shot path. The staged pipeline was reachable only from a jobs-only side panel.

## What changed

**IPC — a run can now start from text (`packages/shared`, `commands/resume_pipeline/`)**
`resumeId`/`jobId` default to empty; `resumeText`, `jobAdText`, `jobTitle`, `companyName`, `board` are accepted alongside them, with zod refinements requiring one of each pair. Resolution is an **id-wins rule**: a non-empty id means a store lookup and a hard error if it's missing — never a silent fallback to the text. `resolve_resume`/`resolve_job` are pure functions taking an id plus an injected lookup closure, so the text isn't even in scope on that path and a miss can only error. `sourceResumeId` is written only on the id path, which is what keeps #990's projects normalization from running against text of unknown provenance. Job-ad text reaches prompts exclusively through the existing `fenced("job_posting", …)` slot, so it inherits ADR-010 injection protection with no new primitive. `jobAdText` is now persisted into the record's `job_ad` (previously left deliberately empty on the text path).

**Retention** — a URL-less pasted job gets its own history slot via a hashed `unlinked_run_key` used only for `RunRow.job_url`, instead of every pasted job sharing one bucket.

**Résumé provenance (`ResumeInputCard`)** — the card surfaces which saved doc backs the current text, so the flow sends `resumeId` when the text is doc-backed and untouched, and `resumeText` once it's hand-edited. Pasted text is never silently imported. The card is seeded from a host-owned `docId` because it remounts on every wizard-step revisit; without the seed a post-remount edit compared against a local `null` and the host kept sending a stale doc id for text the user had since changed.

**TailorFlow runs the staged pipeline** — new `useTailorPipeline` wrapping `useResumePipelineSession`, reconnecting through a persisted run key. Stage events fold into four steps via a pure mapper (`analyze_job|match_evidence|strategy → Analyze`, `draft|cover_letter → Generate`, `validate|repair → Validate`, `humanize → Remove AI signs`; an unknown stage keeps the last). Numbered rows become checkmarks as stages finish, each with a one-line description, the thinking bubble, and the streaming pane. The depth picker is gone from the wizard. The fast-path tailor engine and its store are deleted, dead after the cutover.

## Review findings resolved in-branch

Four Opus reviews ran (rust-backend-architect, tauri-security-reviewer, frontend-reviewer, ui-ux-expert). Two rounds of blocking findings, all fixed and mutation-verified — each guard was reverted, watched go red, and restored:

- **Infinite update loop** — the run-persist effect had an unstable callback in its deps and no already-persisted guard, so persist → store update → new callback identity → refire. Fixed with a keyed guard plus a ref-held callback. The keying is itself asserted, so a legitimate second run still persists.
- **Cross-application run leak** — the persisted run key wasn't tied to an application, so opening application B could reconnect to A's run. Replaced with a self-describing `applyRun: { forId, runId, jobId }` read only when `forId` matches, correct on first render rather than via a reset effect. The reviewer confirmed the router does not remount on a param change, so the pre-existing `key={id}` on the page is a load-bearing part of this — noted for future readers.
- **A raw i18n key in the timed-out banner** — `pipeline.status.*` is `running/completed/needsReview/failed/cancelled` but the panel's own states are `done/needsReview/cancelled/error`, so a timed-out-but-saved run rendered the literal dotted key next to its stop reason, in both locales. The existing test could not catch it: a key-echoing `t` mock is structurally blind to a missing key. Fixed with an exhaustive `Record<TailorRunState, …>` (a new state fails to type-check until mapped) plus a test that asserts every reachable dynamic key against the **real** locale JSON.
- **Focus escaping an open dialog** — the stage-change focus effect fired against an open modal (the focus trap only intercepts Tab, not a programmatic `.focus()`), reachable via "start a run → open Interview questions → run finishes". Now bails when focus is inside `[aria-modal="true"]`, and no longer fires on mount.
- **Contrast** — the "all steps completed" confirmation and the streaming-target header were `text-foreground/45` (4.07:1 dark, below AA and below the `<14px` floor documented in `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`). Both at `/70` now. Every changed colour was independently recomputed in both themes, accounting for the light-scheme opacity lifts.
- Also: the 4th step now actually marks as done (including on the zero-cost humanize path), the panel fits the 900×600 floor with the thinking bubble collapsed by default, an elapsed timer keeps a long stage from looking frozen, a timed-out-but-saved run no longer reads as a clean success, a needsReview run with zero claims has a way forward, screen-reader users get per-row state plus a polite announcer that now also announces completion, and cancelling with no output is acknowledged.

Two items were deliberately left out of scope and are **not** regressions from this PR: the thinking-transcript contrast (3.75:1 light, pre-existing — worth its own ticket) and the elapsed-clock resetting on reconnect. One reviewer claim was refuted rather than acted on: the Cancel button was recomputed at 4.63:1 and passes AA as shipped.

## Testing

`pnpm typecheck` (13/13) · `pnpm test` (488 files / 7118 tests) · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · en/de key parity, zero orphans either direction · full Rust suite green via the pre-push hook.

Known gap, stated rather than papered over: the newly wired completion announcement can't fire in production today, because the panel unmounts before the step counter passes the last step. The durable completion signal is the results panel's own screen-reader line. The branch is wired correctly for when that changes and is covered directly by test.
